exercises.heading: 8.1. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Use the arc length formula (3) to find the length of the curve $$y = 3 - 2x$$ , $$- 1 \leqslant x \leqslant 3$$ . Check your answer by noting that the curve is a line segment and calculating its length by the distance formula.

image.alt: Details A line segment is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The line segment, labeled y = 3 minus 2 x, begins at the point (negative 1, 5), goes down and to the right, and ends at the point (3, negative 3).

problem.paragraph: Use the arc length formula to find the length of the curve $$y = \sqrt{4 - x^{2}}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2$$ . Check your answer by noting that the curve is part of a circle.

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The curve, y = sqrt(4 minus x^2), begins at a marked point (0, 2), goes down to the right, concave down, and ends at a marked point (2, 0).

problem.paragraph: to find the exact length of the arc of the curve $$y = e^{ x}$$ that lies between the points $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$ and $$({2,e^{2}})$$ .

Use either a computer or a table of integrals to find the exact length of the arc of the curve $$y = x^{4 \slash 3}$$ that lies between the points $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ and $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ . If your software has trouble evaluating the integral, make a substitution that changes the integral into one that the software can evaluate.
Find the length of the astroid $$x^{2 \slash 3} + y^{2 \slash 3} = 1$$ .

list.item: Use Formulas 3 and 4 to set up two integrals for the arc length from $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ to $$\left( {1,1} \right)$$ . Observe that one of these is an improper integral and evaluate both of them.
Find the length of the arc of this curve from $$\left( {- 1,1} \right)$$ to $$\left( {8,4} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: Find the arc length function for the curve $$y = 2x^{3 \slash 2}$$ with starting point $$P_{0}(1,2)$$ .

list.item: Find the arc length function for the curve $$y = \ln\left( \sin x \right),0 < x < \pi$$ , with starting point $$\left( {\pi \slash 2,0} \right)$$ .
Graph both the curve and its arc length function on the same screen. Why is the arc length function negative when $$x$$ is less than $$\pi \slash 2$$ ?

problem.paragraph: Find the arc length function for the curve $$y = \sin^{- 1}x + \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}$$ with starting point $$\left( {0,1} \right)$$ .
The arc length function for a curve $$y = f(x)$$ , where $$f$$ is an increasing function, is $${s(x)} = {\int_{0}^{x}{\sqrt{3t + 5}}}dt$$ .

list.item: If $$f$$ has $$y$$ -intercept $$2$$ , find an equation for $$f$$ .
What point on the graph of $$f$$ is $$3$$ units along the curve from the $$y$$ -intercept? State your answer rounded to $$3$$ decimal places.

problem.paragraph: A hawk flying at $$15m \slash s$$ at an altitude of $$180$$ m accidentally drops its prey. The parabolic trajectory of the falling prey is described by the equation

until it hits the ground, where $$y$$ is its height above the ground and $$x$$ is the horizontal distance traveled in meters. Calculate the distance traveled by the prey from the time it is dropped until the time it hits the ground. Express your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a meter.

A steady wind blows a kite due west. The kite’s height above ground from horizontal position $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 80$$ ft is given by $$y = 150 - \frac{1}{40}\left( {x - 50} \right)^{2}$$ . Find the distance traveled by the kite.

A manufacturer of corrugated metal roofing wants to produce panels that are $$28$$ in. wide and $$2$$ in. high by processing flat sheets of metal as shown in the figure. The profile of the roofing takes the shape of a sine wave. Verify that the sine curve has equation $$y = \sin\left( {\pi x \slash 7} \right)$$ and find the width $$w$$ of a flat metal sheet that is needed to make a $$28$$ -inch panel. (Numerically evaluate the integral correct to four significant digits.)

image.alt: Details The figure has two parts. The first part is a rectangular sheet with its longer side labeled w. The second part shows the sheet warped like a wave such that its longer sides resemble a sinusoidal wave. The wave has a length of 28 inches and a height of 2 inches.

exercises.instruction: 48, 49, and 50 Catenary Curves A chain (or cable) of uniform density that is suspended between two points, as shown in the figure, hangs in the shape of a curve called a catenary with equation $$y = a\cos h\left( x\slash a \right)$$ . (See the Discovery Project following Section 12.2.) Details A curve and a horizontal bar are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve is a parabola that begins at a point in the second quadrant, goes down and to the right concave up, reaches a low point labeled a on the positive y axis, goes up and to the right, and ends at a point in the first quadrant. The horizontal bar extends across the top of the graph is positioned such that it touches both ends of the curve.

list.item: Find the arc length of the catenary $$y = a\cos h\left( x\slash a \right)$$ on the interval $$\lbrack c,d\rbrack$$ .
Show that on any interval $$\lbrack c,d\rbrack$$ , the ratio of the area under the catenary to its arc length is $$a$$ .

For the function $$f(x) = \frac{1}{4}e^{ x} + e^{- x}$$ , prove that the arc length on any interval has the same value as the area under the curve.
